Hi Jenny — thanks for the clear context. Short answer: we can give a conservative day-one estimate and a tuned profile after 2–4 weeks of live traffic and a short tuning sprint. Below is a concise breakdown; Connor and Monica are looped for implementation details and SLAs.

Day-one (baseline, minimal tuning)
- Batching: default SDK batching enabled; effective token throughput improvements ~1.1–1.3x vs single-request when traffic is low.
- Caching: no customer-specific prefix/KV cache enabled by default; repeated prompts may still benefit from shared model-level caches.
- Quantization: we will serve the selected open checkpoint in its validated quantized variant if available (typically a conservative int8 profile) — expect modest latency reduction, small degrade in edge-case quality for complex summaries.
- Routing: single-region routing to avoid cross-region hops.
- Expected outcomes: for short prompts, p95 latency ~350–450ms (day-one). Unit token cost at baseline.

Tuned (2–4 weeks after ingestion + tuning sprint)
- Batching: configure continuous batching and request coalescing for UI routes — realistic throughput gains 1.8–2.5x depending on concurrency.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching (TTL tunable) for repeat clinical lookups, recommended TTL 5–30s for UI, longer for background jobs.
- Quantization: test int8 vs mixed-int4 profiles (we usually A/B test int4 in non-critical routes). Latency improvements: additional 10–40% token-time reduction depending on model/hardware.
- Routing: split-by-policy — low-latency zone for UI (SLO backed), cost-tier or burst routing for background jobs. Automatic fallback to higher-capacity cheaper variants during load.
- Expected outcomes: short prompts p95 ~220–300ms, background jobs improved cost per token 20–45% depending on batch profiles.

Immediate blockers to flag to procurement
- HIPAA/data residency: request for Private deployment or VPC peering + KMS for PHI in flight/stored logs.
- Procurement will want an outline of roll-in credits and commit tier to pin Dedicated pools for predictable latency.

Next step: can we schedule a 45-minute tuning kickoff this week? Connor will bring a draft tuning checklist and Monica will outline the rollout & metrics. I attached a short onboarding checklist + the efficiency matrix that Connor will expand on.

Thanks — Aisha

Linking some concrete technical constraints and an initial config recommendation (high-level):

1) Batching & concurrency- baseline: SDK continuous batcher with 50ms coalescing window. For UI routes with 5–20 RPS we typically see 1.5x improvement.
- Recommendation day-one: keep 50ms window, enable per-route batch size cap = 16.
- Recommendation tuned: reduce coalescing window to 20ms on high-traffic UI nodes and enable adaptive batching for background pipelines (cap 64).

2) KV / prefix caching- baseline: disabled for customer-specific keys until we validate determinism on prompt templates.
- Recommendation tuned: enable prefix caching for template-driven calls (e.g., clinical code lookup flows). Start with TTL=10s for UI, 600s for background. Monitor cache hit-rate; target 30–60% hit rate for UI routes to see meaningful latency wins.

3) Quantization profiles- baseline: deploy int8 profile that we've validated for your chosen model; quality regressions are typically rare but must be validated on your eval set.
- Recommendation tuned: run a 2-arm A/B testing window for int4 on background jobs only (non-critical summaries), measure ROUGE/QA pass rates or your QA metric. If pass rate delta <1.5% and latency gain significant, incrementally widen int4 to low-risk routes.

4) Routing & fallback policy- baseline: single region, reserved Dedicated pool (if committed) or hosted with region pin.
- Recommendation tuned: define two policies: "ui-fast" (low-latency, higher cost, strict SLO) and "batch-cost" (cost-optimized, best-effort). Implement automatic fallback: if ui-fast pool p95 > 500ms for 30s, failover to neighboring region/backoff model variant with preserved correctness.

Metrics and instrumentation to prioritize in the first 2 weeks
- Token-level latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) per route
- Cache hit-rate per template and per-user id
- Batch size distribution over time
- Quality regression alerts tied to eval prompts (we'll link to your eval set)

I uploaded an initial efficiency matrix with per-route knobs and expected delta numbers (see attachment). Happy to walk through line-by-line in the kickoff.

Jenny — short answers inline and proposed immediate plan.

HIPAA / deployment model
- Private deployment is the clearest path for PHI at-rest separation; however, VPC + KMS + Private control plane (our Private offering) meets most enterprise controls without full air-gap. For initial rollout (pilot) we can use VPC peering + strict log redaction + KMS; legal often signs off to start with that and move to on-prem/Private for production. We'll draft a one-page legal summary and hand it to your counsel.

Quantization A/B sample size
- Ballpark: for mid-frequency background jobs, ~10k inference calls per arm gives good power for typical QA metrics. For UI short prompts, you can get signals with smaller n (~2–3k) but background metrics are more stable for distributional changes.

Proposed near-term schedule (fast path)
- 2026-11-24: 45-min kickoff (technical + procurement) — Connor to present matrix.
- 2026-11-29 to 2026-12-03: tuning sprint (A/B windows for quantization on non-critical routes; enable caching + adjusted batching on staging).
- 2026-12-06: freeze begins — we will deliver tuned report and recommended production rollout plan before this date.

Action items assigned
- Connor: prepare per-route rollout commands and monitoring dashboards (due 11/24).
- Monica: draft the 1-page legal summary for VPC/KMS vs Private (due 11/23).
- Jenny: please confirm kickoff attendees and whether procurement needs additional artifacts for legal review.
